title: Should College / University Be Free?
description: Luyện nghe và học từ vựng tiếng Anh qua chủ đề tranh luận kinh tế - xã hội: Có nên miễn học phí đại học hay không.
transcript:
In this video we’re going to ask the ___controversial___ question of whether College, also known as university in european countries, should be free. To organize this video, I’m going to use the same 3 ___criteria___ I’ve used in my previous video about universal healthcare, which you can watch by clicking on the link in the description. The criteria will test free college based on its ___universality___, which concerns how much of the population would have access to it, price, which is where the money would actually come from, and finally there is the criteria of quality- Would free college make the degrees better, or worse, or would it not have a difference?

So that’s the criteria, but before we begin, why don’t you like this video and subscribe to my channel for more great content.

The first criteria that we’re going to test free college by is its universality. Free college would be by definition universal, because it would be free and thus anybody could access it. This might lead to more students from low income families entering higher education and graduating, which would improve social ___mobility___. With a more educated ___workforce___, workers may be better able to respond to economic changes with ___revolutionary___ new products, or better business practices, which would be good for economic growth.

Those against free college use the example of the US to argue that the current system of college paid for by ___tuition___ can still be near enough universal. The US has some of the highest college fees in the world but also the highest rates of college ___enrolment___. There is also the question of whether free college would actually help poor families, if rich people continued to be the ones ___disproportionately___ going to college, they would be the ones saving money, not poor families.

Now we’re going to talk about price. If college was free, students would arguably be free of ___crippling___ loans needed to pay for college, which in the US average $30,000 per student. Free from this debt, graduates would be able to buy cars and get on the ___housing___ ladder, improving their ___employability___. There is also the argument that colleges are already getting tax breaks or ___subsidies___ for political reasons, and it would be far simpler to just make tuition free.

Those against free college have a core argument when it comes to price which is that there isn’t really any such thing as ‘free’ college. If students aren’t ___footing___ the bill then the money has to come from tax ___hikes___, on people who are working and who have often have not gone to college. Or there is the option of a graduate tax style system, which is where students pay higher tax than everybody else once they graduate. But this is problematic because it is founded on the idea that all graduates will earn more when they graduate than those who haven’t gone to college, because they tend to end up in ___white-collar___ jobs but this isn’t always true.

Those against free college also argue that students will still have to pay for essentials whilst studying like food and accommodation, and if that was made free, taxes would have to go even higher. Opponents also argue that having to pay off loans teaches students good ___financial___ skills, which puts them in good stead for not ___defaulting___ off payments on cars and mortgages.

The final criteria we’re going to test free college by is the quality of the service provided. Those in favour of free college argue that it would cause students to go for subjects that interest them more, as opposed to ones that they can pay off more easily or are more ___vocational___. This wouldn’t necessarily result in better quality degrees, but it would possibly make students take more care in their degrees and try harder. As well as this, if only a few colleges went free they could compete with private colleges which might provide better quality degrees overall because competing colleges would have to raise their ___standards___ to get more students.

Those against free college argue that it would lead to students being lazy and not taking their degree seriously, because they would not be paying for it. This may then lead to lower quality degrees and a less educated workforce in the long run. Opponents also problematize free college as promoting the notion that the only way to get the best jobs is through getting a degree, whilst in reality a lot of graduates work in low skilled low pay jobs after graduation. There is also the risk, opponents say, of free college leading to the same waiting lists seen in free healthcare systems.

So, to conclude, free college might be a good thing in that it might improve social mobility for the poor, save students thousands in debt, and let them study what they are actually passionate about. Or it would be financially untenable, and would saddle working taxpayers with students’ debts, and would produce low quality degrees. What do you think of free college? Tell me your opinion in the comments section below. Thanks for watching, don’t forget to like, share and subscribe.

mcqQuestions.q: What does the sentence "Free college would be by definition universal, because it would be free and thus anybody could access it" mean?
options: Everyone is legally required to go to university.
Universities will accept all applicants without any entry exams.
Cost would no longer be a barrier preventing anyone from attending college.
Free college is only meant for citizens living in universal healthcare countries.

mcqQuestions.q: What is the main idea of: "With a more educated workforce, workers may be better able to respond to economic changes..."?
options: Educated workers get fired less during economic crises.
Higher education equips workers with skills to innovate and adapt economically.
Economic changes only happen when universities are free.
Workers will refuse to do manual labor during economic changes.

mcqQuestions.q: In the sentence "The US has some of the highest college fees in the world but also the highest rates of college enrolment", what argument is being made?
options: High fees prevent people from going to college in the US.
The US government pays for most students' enrolment.
Students in the US prefer expensive colleges over cheap ones.
College enrolment is high despite high tuition fees, showing free college isn't strictly necessary for high access.

mcqQuestions.q: What does "If rich people continued to be the ones disproportionately going to college, they would be the ones saving money, not poor families" imply?
options: Rich people should be banned from attending free college.
Free college might accidentally subsidize wealthy families more than helping low-income ones.
Poor families do not care about saving money on higher education.
College will automatically become more expensive for rich families.

mcqQuestions.q: What does "Free from this debt, graduates would be able to buy cars and get on the housing ladder..." mean?
options: Housing is provided free of charge to debt-free graduates.
Debt forces students to build houses and buy cars immediately.
Graduates without debt prefer driving cars to going to university.
Eliminating student debt allows young adults to spend money and invest in major life assets, boosting the economy.

mcqQuestions.q: What point is made by "If students aren’t footing the bill then the money has to come from tax hikes..."?
options: Free college actually means shifted costs—taxpayers pay instead of students.
Students will pay their bills directly using tax refund checks.
Tax hikes only affect students who choose to go to free colleges.
Governments can create money out of thin air to fund free college.

mcqQuestions.q: Why is a graduate tax problematic according to: "This is problematic because it is founded on the idea that all graduates will earn more... but this isn’t always true"?
options: Graduates refuse to pay taxes after getting their degrees.
It unfairly assumes every graduate lands a high-paying job, which isn't always the case.
Low-skilled workers earn more than all university graduates.
Graduate taxes are illegal in most European countries.

mcqQuestions.q: What does "Having to pay off loans teaches students good financial skills" suggest?
options: Taking out student loans makes people expert accountants.
Repaying debt instills financial discipline and responsibility early in life.
Students who do not take loans will inevitably go bankrupt.
Loan companies offer free financial skill training to all borrowers.

mcqQuestions.q: What is meant by "Competing colleges would have to raise their standards to get more students"?
options: Free options force private universities to improve quality to remain attractive.
Free colleges will shut down due to intense private competition.
Universities will raise tuition costs to make degrees look higher quality.
Standards will drop everywhere because competition becomes too easy.

mcqQuestions.q: What warning is expressed in: "Opponents also argue that it would lead to students being lazy and not taking their degree seriously..."?
options: Free college causes physical laziness and health problems in youth.
Professors will stop grading lazy students in free universities.
Students will choose easy majors to avoid studying long hours.
Without personal financial investment, students might value their education less and put in less effort.
